headline: 5 Costly Home Remodeling Mistakes to Avoid When Planning Your Layout
articleBody:
Rushing into an interior remodeling project without ironclad preparation is the fastest path to budget overruns and construction headaches. Here are five frequent remodeling mistakes homeowners encounter and practical ways to bypass them.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

1. Starting work before pulling permits: Assuming small layout alterations do not require municipal approval is risky. Structural changes, relocated plumbing, or new electrical circuits require building department permits and inspections to ensure code compliance. Always verify permit needs before demolition begins.

2. Using vague allowance budgets: Selecting generic line items for cabinetry, tile, or countertops often leads to price shock later. Choose your primary materials and finish fixtures before construction starts so your estimate reflects actual costs.

3. Skipping trade sequencing: Drywall, electrical rough-ins, and plumbing must happen in a strict physical order. Closing up walls before trade rough-ins pass inspection results in costly tear-outs and rework.

4. Overlooking written change orders: Agreeing to verbal modifications on site makes it difficult to track your final balance. Insist that all scope modifications include written costs and schedule impacts.

5. Hiring uninsured or unlicensed labor: Always verify active liability and workers' compensation policies before letting crews on site.
